text:
Today marks a huge milestone for my social media career, 20k Instagram followers.

Doubling my followers in 30 days and on track to hit 100 million views in 30 days. However, I’ve taken away quite a few lessons. I’ll keep it simple:

1. Overcoming the fear of judgement.

2. Consistency. Consistency. Consistency.

3. Virality is inconsistent.

It’s very easy to get caught up in KPI’s such as views, follows, comments, shares. It’s also good to note that you will never always have great responses (as I also had over 1000 unfollows last month). But what’s important is to keep moving forward.

text:
This past Friday I had the opportunity to shadow Sydney Kuby with the Dallas Mavericks!!

Not only was this an amazing experience I learned a lot of invaluable things including: 

The importance of timeliness and authenticity when speaking to clients. The high involvement of the sales team at games with customer experience, and the emphasis on relationship over transaction. Finally, the togetherness of the team with the fun and motivating environment of the staff. A competitive and encouraging environment fosters growth and continuity within the team.

Thank you again to Kyle Gillespy for setting things up! Also thank you to Baylor S3E for initializing this interaction that gave me this opportunity!

text:
These past 75 days, I have created UGC for Creed, a Bible Chat and Companion App. Here’s what I’ve learned:

1. 📈 KPI’s: Data. That’s what really matters, right? In my first 75 days I have officially received over 11M views, nearly 1.5M likes, 15k comments, and over 40k shares. I created this account from scratch that now has 4k followers on it. Creed, having launched in September 2025 now bodes over 75,000 daily users and 500,000 downloads.

2. 💡 How to Perform: The social media industry is a very fast-paced industry. With trends coming and going within days, knowing when to innovate or when to mirror previous success is important. Finding similar content to the content you want to create can really help. But what else plays a role besides a trending audio or caption you may ask?

3. 🤖 Learning Algorithms: Each platform has its own unique algorithm. Posting times, engagements such as comments, shares, and reposts, and “priming your account” are indicative of your account’s performance that are often overlooked. A poor posting schedule or posting as soon as you create an account can flag your account as a bot account.

4. 🗓️ Consistency: With this fast paced environment, it is important that you continue creating content. Posting 3x a day, my consistency was rewarded. Replying to comments on a video can become very tedious and time-consuming, but can vastly change the outcome of a video.

5. 📖 My Faith: As someone who is Unapologetically Christian, countless conversations about my faith in comment sections, personal DM’s, and with friends have really encouraged me to continue finding ways to spread the Word.

Christianity Today feature: https://lnkd.in/gRFZjcrc

PS: This wasn’t written by AI

I am looking forward to gaining hands-on experience in sports and entertainment marketing, social media marketing, and active collaboration. I am very grateful for this opportunity to learn, grow, and work alongside sports media personalities such as John Morris, Ward Whites, Jacob Bumpas, former NFL cornerback Gary Baxter, and former Dallas Cowboys scout Glenn Smith!

A big thank you to Riley Walker for this great opportunity!!
